key_insight: Combined computational and neural-network modelling identified a defect-free HDPE friction stir welding window, with optimal tested conditions of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-map development to reduce weld defects and stabilize forces when joining HDPE.
method: Simulated temperature, force, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Trained two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Validated simulations experimentally and combined modelling approaches to map weldability.
evidence_signal: ANN predictions achieved R² of 0.91–0.99; 60 °C bottom preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to about 1100 N and raised peak temperature from 70 °C to about 100 °C.
watch_item: Prediction accuracy and optimal settings are supported within the tested parameter space; transfer to other HDPE grades or welding setups requires validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
